rec3.observations: No visible drag indicator while reaching around the incapacitated patient.

root_cause: Native medic fixture set medic and patient to team 0, while the client retained medic team 1 from its join roster. Friendly-only drag selection, revival indicator, repair status and the drag marker therefore rejected the ally. Real network render reproduced the mismatch; after projecting native teams into client presentation, both are team 0 and the marker renders.
changes: Native snapshot class presentation carries team and updates player team state. Fixture server metadata also matches native teams.
Physical transport steering is explicitly enabled by default, saved as a VR control preference, with an optional stick fallback.
CQ gloves remain children of their tracked controllers; the competing XRTools physics transform update is disabled. Free transport passenger hands follow late seat correction.
Cabin repair tool mount is fixed to the front passenger dashboard at seat offset (0, 0.95, -0.55), independent of tracked head motion.
Massacre charge messages render on a 320x200 texture inside the authored monitor glass. Display is parented to the actual gun and inherits weapon scale, recoil and late tracking.
Small medic drag ring faces the viewer and renders over patient armour/weapons; world cover still blocks it. Visible within 3 m.
User confirmed interactions work correctly and requested only the small neck grab marker. The large revival indicator is removed from CQ rendering; its legacy preview is isolated from gameplay.

large_indicator_removal.note: Presentation-only removal followed the full integration run.

known_diagnostics: Existing isolated fixture ObjectDB/resource shutdown diagnostics.

live_test.status: Technician OpenXR client connected; fixture ready

launch.reset: F8 or RESET TECHNICIAN TEST in the menu
